classification.difficultyReason: Generate coterminal angles by adding or subtracting full rotations and recognise that this can continue indefinitely.

children.label: a
children.prompt: List 6 possible angles of inclination that this ray could represent.

spec.description: Perpendicular axes with arrowheads at both ends, without ticks or axis names. A blue segment joins the blue origin point to a blue endpoint in the first quadrant. A black 30° label lies between the segment and the positive horizontal axis.
spec.mathematics: The ray has inclination 30° and represents every angle differing from 30° by an integer multiple of 360°.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent given diagram; no answers are shown.

answer.worked:
Add or subtract $360^{\circ}$ repeatedly:
$$\begin{aligned}30^{\circ}+360^{\circ}&=390^{\circ}\\390^{\circ}+360^{\circ}&=750^{\circ}\\30^{\circ}-360^{\circ}&=-330^{\circ}\\-330^{\circ}-360^{\circ}&=-690^{\circ}\\-690^{\circ}-360^{\circ}&=-1050^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$$
Together with $30^{\circ}$, these give six possible angles. In general, $\theta=30^{\circ}+360^{\circ}n$, where $n$ is an integer.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Is there a limit to how many angles this ray could represent?

answer.worked: No. Adding or subtracting $360^{\circ}$ gives another angle represented by the same ray, and this can continue indefinitely.
